**Finding submitted: deviation (critical rule IP), confidence 0.86.**

**What I found in § 4:**

1. **Ownership conditioned on payment (§ 4(a), p0017)** — the Works are ours only "to the extent that such Works were created ... over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid." Title therefore never vests on creation, and there is no present assignment — only a duty to give "reasonably required assistance," at *our* cost. Contractor would hold IP in any deliverable not yet invoiced/paid.

2. **No Customer Data / pre-existing IP ownership provision** — our data appears only as "Confidential Information" in § 8 (p0038) and as a warranty carve-out in § 5(b) (p0025). Nothing confirms we retain title, and nothing bars joint ownership.

3. **Licence back is short of preferred (§ 4(c), p0021)** — perpetual, royalty-free and sublicensable, but neither irrevocable nor worldwide, so embedded Contractor IP in our deliverables is theoretically revocable.

**Not flagged:** § 4(b) (p0019–p0020), where Contractor retains its own proprietary tools, methodologies and know-how not created for us. That is expressly acceptable under the rule ("Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine") and I left it intact.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** ownership vests on creation with an express irrevocable assignment decoupled from invoicing; new § 4(e) confirming Company Data and Company IP remain ours with only a service-performance licence to Contractor and no joint ownership; and "worldwide ... irrevocable" added to the § 4(c) licence. Each edit is a targeted substring change rather than a rewrite of the section.
